It pinned a KNOWN DEFECT and now pins the fix (SPEC Q17). `upi-debit-vpa` ended the merchant group on `(?:\.|\bon\b|\bUPI\b|\bRef\b|$)` with a leading `\s*` that could match zero characters. `@` is a non-word character, so a VPA using the NPCI handle `@upi` put a word boundary immediately before it and the alternation fired *inside the address*: `kirana@upi` was captured as `kirana@`. The word alternatives now require real whitespace in front of them (`\s+(?:on|UPI|Ref)\b`), so they can only end the merchant at a token boundary, never mid-address. The expectation below is the corrected capture. Found by the P2-9 corpus expansion, not by a user; `upi-credit-vpa` carried the same tail and was fixed with it.
